receipt.public_excerpt: DeepSeek-R1 achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 on reasoning tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: The developer reports comparable reasoning performance from a competing model, supporting the narrower proposition that frontier capabilities can be matched. This does not measure customer switching, persistent pricing power, or the durability of any advantage.

evidence_items.locator: Page 9, section 3.2, Fact 2, discussion of Claude 3.7 Sonnet
evidence_items.explanation: The study finds that adoption of Claude 3.7 mainly displaced its predecessor rather than competing models, cautioning against treating models as interchangeable commodities. Its January–April sample extends beyond the target period, so it is context rather than decisive outcome evidence.

evidence_items.locator: Executive Summary, Areas to Watch, item 2
evidence_items.explanation: The FTC identifies possible contractual and technical barriers in cloud partnerships with AI developers. These qualify any inference that the entire AI market lacks barriers, but concern developers switching cloud providers rather than customers switching LLMs.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not establish whether model-specific advantages or pricing power were durable in the target period.
The comparable-performance result is developer-reported and covers reasoning tasks rather than all economically relevant uses.
The customer-usage study covers only OpenRouter and extends into April 2025.
No reviewed evidence jointly measures representative customer switching, model differentiation, entry barriers, and sustained margins or pricing power.
Evidence of falling prices or benchmark convergence would not by itself separate competitive pressure from technological cost reductions or establish the absence of a moat.
